name: Anthocyanins / bilberry extract
short: Serious adverse events were rare in a small ulcerative colitis trial; an 8-week office-worker trial had no severe ones. A 28-day pre-post study in 26 healthy adults found reduced platelet aggregation.
text: In an 8-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of bilberry extract in office workers aged 20 to 40, there were no severe adverse events in either group. In a randomised, placebo-controlled trial of an anthocyanin-rich extract from bilberries in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis, which ended early with 34 patients randomised, serious adverse events were rare; the abstract does not give their number or compare them between groups. In a study of 26 healthy adults who took anthocyanin capsules for 28 days, with no control group described, ADP-stimulated platelet aggregation and blood fibrinogen fell significantly; the authors framed this as a possible reduction in thrombotic risk, and the abstract does not report on bleeding. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
